createdBy: claude (found while sampling real zug tail output for landing copy)
impact:
Five of 180 records in observations.jsonl have the remainder of the caller's tool-call block serialised into the `observation` string value. Affected lines 176-180, all dated 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21. Observed leaked fragments: `</observation>`, `<parameter name="pattern">` followed by the pattern text, and in the newest record `</invoke>`.

Reproduce: `zug tail 2` renders the garbage inline, e.g. a record ending `...experimental discipline (...).</observation>\n</invoke>` and another ending `...retained with the axis they failed on.</observation>\n<parameter name="pattern">converges by accumulating rejection criteria`.

Correlation worth checking first: every affected record is a call that also supplied the optional `pattern` argument, and all five are recent. That points at argument serialisation on the client side rather than at storage, but Zug is where the damage lands and where it can be caught.

Why it matters beyond cosmetics: observations.jsonl is the input to synthesis. src/synthesize.ts feeds these strings into the PERSONA and PLAYBOOK prompts, so the model is being shown XML-ish tool-call fragments as if they were content. That risks the model echoing markup back into PERSONA.md, and it inflates the token cost of every synthesis. It also corrupts recurrence matching if the trailing text lands in the value used for pattern comparison.

Suggested fix: validate and strip in zug_save_observation before append. Reject or trim anything from the first `</observation>`, `<parameter`, `</invoke>` or `</` onward, and consider failing loudly rather than silently storing, so a malformed caller is visible instead of quietly polluting the corpus. A one-off repair pass over the five existing records is also needed; they are already in the synthesis input.
resolution:
Fixed client-side (371ac20), deployed to Fly as v46, canonical store repaired and verified end to end.

**Shipped**

`stripToolCallMarkup` / `sanitizeObservation` in src/storage.ts, applied in both write paths: `appendObservation` and `addObservations` (the sync merge). Truncates at the first marker rather than deleting matches, since the leak is always a tail. A record made only of markup is left intact rather than emptied, because truncation cannot repair it and a silent empty string is worse than a visible bad one. `zug_save_observation` warns in its response when it strips, so a malformed caller is told rather than quietly cleaned up after. `zug repair [--dry-run]` added and documented.

**Why the merge path mattered**

Dedupe is on `timestamp|observation`. A repaired local record would no longer have matched its corrupt twin arriving from the server, so a pull would have appended both and a push would have sent the repaired one as an extra row: repairing locally on a synced install would have doubled every record it fixed. Sanitizing on ingest makes them compare equal. Test: "cleans incoming records so a pull cannot reintroduce the corrupt twin".

**Canonical repair**

Canonical store is `/data/.zug/users/default/.zug/` (multi-tenant layout: `ZUG_USERS_ROOT=/data/.zug/users`), not `ZUG_DATA_DIR` directly, so the repair had to be run with `ZUG_DATA_DIR` pointed at the tenant directory.

- Backed up in place to `observations.jsonl.pre-iss057` on the volume before touching anything.
- Pre-repair file was byte-identical to the local pre-repair copy (116957 bytes), confirming the server held the same corruption.
- Applied: 180 scanned, 5 repaired, 180 records still present, `grep` for markup returns 0, second dry-run reports 0 corrupted.

**End-to-end verification**

`zug sync` round-trip after the repair returned `{"push":{"status":"ok"},"pull":{"status":"ok"}}`, and the local corpus stayed at 180 records with 0 corrupted. That exercises the dedupe-after-sanitize path against real data on both sides, which was the risk.

Server health: v46 started, `/mcp` returns 401 as expected for an unauthenticated request.

**Backups retained**

- local: `~/.zug/observations.jsonl.pre-iss057-20260920222206`
- server: `/data/.zug/users/default/.zug/observations.jsonl.pre-iss057`

**Root cause still unaddressed**

This fixes the damage and prevents recurrence in storage, not the leak itself. All five affected calls also passed `pattern` and all landed within roughly 30 hours, which points at client-side argument serialisation rather than anything in Zug. Filing a separate issue is not obviously useful since the defect is likely outside this repo, but if new corrupt records appear after 2026-09-21 the sanitizer will now say so in the tool response, which is the signal to look again.
title: zug_save_observation stores trailing tool-call markup inside the observation text
